metadata.consistency_ledger:
# BINDING CONSISTENCY LEDGER — Croatian Listening Pod (15 scenes)

## TRANSLITERATION
Not needed — names stay as written in Latin script.

## PRICES
- £8.40 → osam eura četrdeset
- £2.50 → dva eura pedeset
- £12.50 → dvanaest eura pedeset

## TARGET-LANGUAGE NAME
hrvatski (everyday term for the Croatian language)

## RECURRING LINES

| Canonical | Croatian rendering |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Good morning. What can I get you? | Dobro jutro. Što mogu donijeti? |
| What can I get you? | Što mogu donijeti? |
| Good evening. What can I get you? | Dobar večer. Što mogu donijeti? |
| I'd like a [item], please. | Želim [item], molim. |
| Could I pay by card? | Mogu karticu? |
| Do you have contactless? | Imate li beskontaktno? |
| Thank you very much. Goodbye. | Hvala vam puno. Doviđenja. |
| Yes, of course. | Da, naravno. |
| Excuse me. | Izvini/Izvinite. |
| Would you like to sit-in or takeaway? | Želiš li da ostaneš ili da ponese? |
| I'm learning Croatian. | Učim hrvatski. |
| You speak very good Croatian. | Vrlo dobro govoriš hrvatski. |
| Thank you. You've been very helpful. | Hvala. Bio si od velike pomoći. |
| I'm on holiday. | Na sam godišnjem odmoru. |

## REGISTER
- **Peer / friend exchanges** (Scenes 1, 4, 5, 6, 15): *ti* + first name (unmarked colloquial)
- **Service staff / customer** (Scenes 3, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 14): *ti* for younger/regular staff; *Vi* for hotel receptionist (Scene 11) and pharmacist (Scene 12, formal context)
- **Stranger interactions** (Scenes 2, 13): *ti* + polite form (*molim*, *izvolite*)
